item.title: Bacterial growth phases reflect changing population physiology
item.content: In a closed batch culture, the classical sequence is lag, exponential (log), stationary, and death/decline phases, reflecting adaptation, rapid division, resource limitation, and loss of viable cells.
item.explanationMarkdown:
The phases are not simply labels for elapsed time:

- **Lag**: cells adapt; division may be limited even though metabolism is active.
- **Exponential/log**: population increases at an approximately constant maximal rate under the conditions.
- **Stationary**: net population growth levels off as nutrients become limiting and wastes accumulate.
- **Death/decline**: viable cell numbers decrease.

The exact shape depends on organism and culture conditions.

cards.prompt: Name the classical phases of a closed bacterial batch culture and summarize what characterizes each.
cards.answerGuidance: Lag: adaptation; exponential/log: rapid approximately constant-rate division; stationary: net growth levels off under limitations; death/decline: viable population decreases.
